newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds weaken ahead of new 10-year supply.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds weaken ahead of new 10-year supply.

text.p: German Bunds came under pressure in late Monday trade with the prospect of fresh supply from a new 10-year issue due on Tuesday.
"The market is a little bit unhappy here," said Dirk Aufderheide at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell futures and options in Frankfurt.
"There is a bit hedging pressure coming through ahead of the new Bund announcement tomorrow."
By 1500 GMT, the DTB June Bund future was 36 basis points lower at 100.46, breaching key support at 100.50. The 10-year benchmark cash Bund was at 100.90 for a 5.886 percent yield.

Dealers also said a number of curve-steepening trades put on over the session were taking the shine off the Bund future, with players selling out of that contract into the BOBL contract and the short end of the cash market.
The five-to-10-year yield spread stood at 125 basis points by 1511 GMT.

But with a good band of technical support in the 100.40 to 100.50 region, analysts said the futures contract should pull back from its lows on Wednesday, particularly with U.S. Treasuries holding up relatively well.
"As soon as the issue is out of the way, we whould see some kind of recovery on the back of the stable U.S. markets," said Aufderheide.
EMU jitters in the French debt market, where the June notionnel contract was also under pressure, were also weighing on Bunds, analysts said.

French President Jacques Chirac is due to appear on national television at 1800 GMT amid strong speculation that he will call an early general election in a bid to avoid a later election clashing with the qualifying period for monetary union.

But the French cash market still managed a better performance on international yield spreads, losing only one basis point on the 10-year gap to Bunds while the German market was in turn outclassed to the tune of six basis points by U.S. Treasuries. By 1527 GMT, the 10-yeat T-note/Bund spread was at 108 basis points versus 114 at Friday's close.
